title: Inquest looks into death after arrest in Kelowna
article: An inquest has begun looking into the death of a Kelowna man after he was arrested by RCMP.
Brandt Jason Zimmer died in the emergency ward of Kelowna General Hospital August 15, 2010, after being arrested for causing a disturbance at a local business.
Zimmer was only wearing his underwear when he entered the Grand Prix family fun centre on Stremel Road. Staff called police, saying he appeared delirious and was yelling at customers.
RCMP arrested the 40-year-old man and took him to KGH, where he subsequently died.
An investigation found Zimmer, who suffered from substance abuse, was under the influence of drugs before he died.
Because Zimmer died while in police custody, Central Saanich Police were brought in to complete a independent review of the RCMP's actions that day.
The investigation determined police did nothing wrong during the arrest.
Coroner Rodrick Mackenzie and a jury will hear evidence from subpoenaed witnesses for the next four days at the Kelowna courthouse.
The jury does not make any findings of legal responsibility, but makes recommendations aimed at preventing deaths under similar circumstances in the future.
